segments: File operations deal with "where things are," and process management deals with "what is running." This article covers "what is inside" and "how the machine is doing."

less — browse one page at a time

head and tail — view the beginning and end
tail -f — follow the end of a file in real time
An excellent tool for watching logs. Press Ctrl+C to stop following.
How to read the output of free -h:
Look at available, not free. Linux uses idle memory for caching, so a small free value with a large available value is normal.
ip — inspect network interfaces (replaces the older ifconfig command)
ss — see what is listening on ports (replaces the older netstat command)
curl — make HTTP requests from the command line
